messages.subject: Error in lav_syntax_parse_rhs(rhs = rhs.formula[[2L]], op = op) :
parts:
Hello all,

 

I am trying to fit a structure equation model, and I get an error message mentioned in the subject. Below I provide a detail of my situation.

 

I’m   totally blind, and therefore, cannot independently use IBM AMOS or any other program for SEM that requires the user to first draw a model using the mouse, and then estimate the model.

 

So, Lavaan and R are a perfect solution for me, as, I do not have to first draw the graph in order for the software to estimate the model. However, before this evening, I had never use Lavaan, and for reasons that I cannot work out, I’m  receiving  an error  message when I try to fit SEM.

 

I am pasting the output of R command line interface below, and next to the # sign are   my questions.

 

 

> library(lavaan)

This is lavaan 0.5-23.1097

lavaan is BETA software! Please report any bugs.

> test = read.csv(file="abc.csv",head=TRUE,sep=",")#load a file that has two independent variables and a continuous  outcome variable.

> model <- ' #start to define the model following the example  provided in Lavaan tutorial on the Lavaan website.

+ ACWater =~ q55 + q59 + q63 + q66#the first independent variable has four indicators so  tell Lavaan the names of the indicators for the first IV.

+ PNWater =~ q50 + q53 + q56 + q61# tell Lavaan the four indicators of the second IV.

+ Water =~ dv # give a name to the continuous  outcome variable.

+ dv ~ ACWater +PNWater # perform regression with two predictors and the dv.

+ q55 ~~ q50 ~~ q59 ~~ q53 ~~ q63 ~~ q56 ~~ q66 ~~ q61 #ask for covariance as shown in the tutorial. Use ~~ operator  to request for covariance.

+ '

> fit = sem(model, data=test) # fit a model, bt the model gives a following error message. What I’m doing wrong. The complete model I want to run has around ten independent variables, I just used two so I can first become familiar with Lavaan. But, I do not know, what is my error, and why the model is not being  estimated.

Error in lav_syntax_parse_rhs(rhs = rhs.formula[[2L]], op = op) :

  lavaan ERROR: I'm confused parsing this line: ~~q50 ~ ~q59 ~ ~q53 ~ ~q63 ~ ~q5

6~q66

> 

 

Any help will be greatly appreciatd.

 

Regards,

Faiz.

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Error in lav_syntax_parse_rhs(rhs = rhs.formula[[2L]], op = op) :
parts: I do not know exactly what model you were trying to estimate, but the problem with your syntax very likely comes from this line of code:
q55 ~~ q50 ~~ q59 ~~ q53 ~~ q63 ~~ q56 ~~ q66 ~~ q61 #ask for covariance as shown in the tutorial. Use ~~ operator  to request for covariance.

lavaan syntax lines feature 1 operator per line. This code uses the ~~ or variance / covariance operator repeatedly, and that will cause problems.

If you are attempting to allow resd=idual covariance between pairs of indicators, then break this line up onto multiple lines of code:

q55 ~~ q50
q59 ~~ q53
q63 ~~ q56
q66 ~~ q61 #ask for covariance as shown in the tutorial. Use ~~ operator  to request for covariance.

Be warned that trying to estimate too many residual covariances may make the model "not identified," so that there are no unique best estimates. You may need to provide starting values to get even this modified model to run.

On the other hand, if your intent was to allow residual covariance among all 8 indicators, that model will not be identified.

--Ed Rigdon

Thank you very much for your reply.

Your reply has helped to clarify source of my problem.

However, now,I have another question:

Does Lavaan automatically calculates covariance matrix, or we have
to include a syntax in the model syntax asking for covariance matrix.

I read that covariance matrix is required when a model is
estimated, so, I was typing q55 ~~ q50 with an assumption that I'm
supplying the code for covariance matrix to the software. Your post
has made it clear to me that I was working under an incorrect
assumption.
But, I'd like to know now, that should I ask Lavaan for covariance
matrix, or it'll compute it automatically.

In the model I was trying to estimate, ACWater and PNWater are the
independent variables, and dv is the dependent variable.

Regards,
Faiz.

messages.subject: Re: Error in lav_syntax_parse_rhs(rhs = rhs.formula[[2L]], op = op) :
parts:
Faiz--
     Yes, the software will compute the necessary moments (covariance matrix and means, if necesary) in the background, when you supply the data. There are statistical reasons why it is better to provide the data itself, rather than giving lavaan a covariance matrix only. And there is, generally, no advantage in providing only a covariance matrix. The exception might be when sample size is very large, and you expect to run several different models. Then you might save computing time by computing the covariance matrix once (using the R cov() function, for example), instead of having lavaan compute it each tim a model is run.
Ed Rigdon
